Team —

Draft attached: rto-rpo-matrix.xlsx (summary below). Notes are based on recent runs and conservative extrapolation for cold starts.

Summary (typical / worst-case):
- Ephemeral inference (stateless requests): RTO = 30s / 6m, RPO = 0 (no persistent state). Explanation: routing and cache warmup typically restore streaming within ~30s; pathological cases where control-plane reconciliation is delayed can take several minutes.
- Stateful embeddings index (incremental index updates): RTO = 6m / 2h, RPO = 0–15m depending on replication lag and last commit window. If weights need to be reloaded and index rebuild is required, worst-case is longer (see matrix).
- Model weights reload scenario (cold boot of model on new region): additional 3–12 minutes typical / 30–90 minutes worst-case for very large weights on constrained networks. We recommend pre-warmed replicas for production-critical models.

Manual steps: cross-region activation requires a single-authorizer approval via Console (role: ProdOps- approver). We can optionally wire a zero-touch policy for enterprise customers after a runbook-validated rehearsal and signed acceptance.

I'll include the matrix and a short rationale paragraph in Naomi's outgoing.

–Neha

Attachment: rto-rpo-matrix.xlsx

Alan —

Appended below is a consolidated response to your four asks. Attached are two artifacts we referenced (redwood-cutover-runbook-v2.pdf, rto-rpo-matrix.xlsx). If you'd like a short walk-through we'll make time for a 30-minute technical sync.

1) Expected end-to-end cutover timeline (detection -> full production traffic):
- Typical (automated detection + warmed standby): 1–3 minutes to detect + 30–90 seconds for routing and health-check validation -> traffic fully routed to standby in under 5 minutes.
- Typical (cold standby): detection 1–3 min + model weight activation and cache warmup 3–12 minutes -> full production traffic typically within 6–15 minutes.
- Worst-case (network congestion / storage rehydration): up to 2 hours while we rebuild stateful indexes or rehydrate from cold backups. We include clear state transition indicators in the Console so customers can track progress.

2) RTO / RPO commitments by workload class (summary):
- Stateless inference: RTO target 30s (SLO), worst-case 6min; RPO 0.
- Embeddings index (replicated): RTO target 6min, worst-case 2h; RPO typically 0–15min depending on commit frequency.
- Model weights cold-boot: add 3–12min typical; worst-case add 30–90min.

3) Manual steps & approvals for cross-region activation:
- Default: a single ProdOps approver in customer tenancy authorizes activation via Console (UI + API). The approval is audited and reversible for the first 30 minutes.
- Zero-touch option: After an agreed rehearsal and signed acceptance, we can enable an automated failover policy that requires no manual approval (recommended for customers with strict RTO requirements).
- For private/on-prem deployments we provide a documented runbook with exact commands and role binding snippets; a named operator must perform the activation unless zero-touch is enabled.

4) Evidence and rehearsals:
- Last full rehearsal: 2027-02-10 (multi-region failover, successful cutover with warmed replicas; post-mortem attached).
- Artifacts attached: redwood-cutover-runbook-v2.pdf (excerpt showing detection rules and transition states) and rto-rpo-matrix.xlsx (detailed numbers and assumptions).

Next steps / ask of Cloudline:
- Confirm whether you want "zero-touch" enabled for the production slices we discussed. If yes, we will schedule a joint rehearsal and produce a signed acceptance memo required to enable the policy.
- If you prefer manual approval, tell us the role(s) for approvers and we'll pre-provision RBAC links for your tenancy.

Thanks — happy to walk through any particular scenario on a quick call.

Best regards,
